headline: Brooks beats Sneyd 5-3 at the Grand Slam and admits he was once lazy
standfirst: Bradley Brooks opened Group M with a win over close friend Carl Sneyd and now plays Gian van Veen for a last-16 place.
body: Bradley Brooks began his Grand Slam of Darts campaign with a 5-3 victory over his friend Carl Sneyd in Wolverhampton, leaving a winner-takes-all meeting with Gian van Veen in the final Group M game.

Brooks said he was pleased with his scoring but felt he let several legs slip on the doubles, which made the contest tighter than it might have been. He was quick to credit Sneyd, saying the Englishman stayed in touch and took the chances he was given, according to Dartsnews.
The pair know each other well, sharing Super League and county darts and travelling together on the ProTour. Brooks said it is never pleasant to face a friend, but accepted it is part of the job.

Afterwards he reflected candidly on his career. He won his first PDC Tour Card at 17 but lost it more than once and had to earn it back. "I'll be the first to admit I was lazy. I didn't practise," he told reporters, adding that he had assumed praise for his ability would be enough.

A year away from the tour, spent playing on the MODUS Super Series, changed that outlook. Seeing other players post about their ProTour weekends made him realise what he was missing, and he has since regained his card and rebuilt his form. He says his practice is now purposeful rather than casual.
With only the group winner advancing, Brooks and Van Veen will meet with a place in the knockout stage at stake.
